question: Chhannulal Mishra, who passed away in October 2025, was known for his contributions in which of the following fields?
solution:
The correct answer is __**हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत (Hindustani Classical Music)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Chhannulal Mishra** was a legendary doyen of **Hindustani Classical Music**, specifically representing the **Kirana Gharana** and the **Banaras Gharana** of **Varanasi**.
 
• He was renowned for his unique ability to perform a wide range of musical genres, including **Khayal**, **Thumri**, **Dadra**, **Kajri**, **Chaiti**, and **Bhajans**.
 
• Born on **August 3, 1936**, in **Hariharpur**, **Azamgarh** district of **Uttar Pradesh**, he moved to **Varanasi** to dedicate his life to the spiritual and classical musical traditions of the holy city.
 
• In recognition of his unparalleled contribution to the arts, he was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award, in the year **2020**.
 
• His passing in **October 2025** marked the end of an era for the **Purab-Ang Gayaki**, a specialized style of singing prevalent in eastern **Uttar Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Musical Lineage and Training:**

 
 
• He received his initial training from his father, **Badri Prasad Mishra**, and later refined his skills under the guidance of **Ustad Abdul Ghani Khan** of the **Kirana Gharana**.
 
• He was also a disciple of **Thakur Jaidev Singh**, who was a great musicologist and philosopher, helping **Chhannulal Mishra** integrate deep spiritual meaning into his renditions.
 
 
 
• **The Banaras Style (Gayaki):**
 
 
• The **Banaras Gharana** is famous for its semi-classical forms like **Thumri** and **Dadra**. Pandit Mishra was often called the "King of Thumri" for his emotive and soulful expressions.
 
• His repertoire also included **Ramcharitmanas** recitals, where he would sing verses in classical ragas, making the epic accessible to common people while maintaining technical purity.
 
 
 
• **Major Awards and Honors:**
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan**: Awarded in **2010** for his distinguished service in the field of **Classical Music**.
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**: Conferred in **2000** by India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• **Yash Bharti Award**: Conferred by the Government of **Uttar Pradesh** for his cultural impact on the state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cultural Impact:** **Pandit Chhannulal Mishra** was instrumental in preserving the **Kajri** (monsoon songs) and **Hori** (songs for Holi), ensuring these folk-classical traditions were showcased on global platforms.
 
• **Discography and Performance:** He performed at various national and international festivals, including the **Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh** in **Varanasi** and the **Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav** in **Pune**.
 
• **Spiritual Connection:** A staunch devotee of Lord **Rama**, his most famous **Bhajans** such as "Jab Se Ram Naam Kahal" and "Balam Re" are considered masterpieces of devotional **Hindustani Classical Music**.
 
• **Legacy:** He is survived by a rich legacy of students and recordings that continue to serve as a textbook for learners of the **Banaras style** of singing.
